newsitem.title: JAPAN: New proposals but same deadline in insurance talks.
newsitem.headline: New proposals but same deadline in insurance talks.

text.p: Japan has put forward significant new proposals aimed at settling a dispute with the United States over the Japanese insurance market, and the two sides will keep their self-imposed Sunday deadline, acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Saturday.
In a briefing to reporters after talks with Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, Barshefsky said: "The deadline is firm and fixed and will not change."
While she was due to leave Japan later on Saturday, Barshefsky said working-level talks would continue between the two nations.

"The Japanese government put forward new proposals which are potentially quite significant in nature. But because it's a complex area and the proposals are new, we need to evaluate them and make a determination whether the primary sector deregulation is sufficient," she said.

A key issue in the dispute is Japan's reluctance to open the biggest areas of its insurance market to outside companies while wanting to allow more domestic firms into a niche sector where foreign firms have the edge.
